rubrics.justification: Description is broadly consistent with a Day 5 2BB blastocyst: visible blastocoel, loosely grouped ICM, and relatively sparse/loose TE. It appropriately notes image/focal limitations and avoids major fabrication, though some comments about possible fragmentation/degeneration are speculative.
Thoroughly integrates age, tubal factor, ovarian reserve/response, BMI, endometrial thickness, semen parameters, and first-cycle status with embryo grade to contextualize prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: intermediate embryo quality tempered by favorable patient factors. Probability estimate follows the discussion, though the opening stray text and slightly optimistic framing of a 2BB as 'good-quality' are minor issues.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based: single embryo transfer at age 31, standard luteal support, no bed rest, and attention to hydrosalpinx are guideline-concordant. PGT-A discussion is appropriately cautious, though mentioning it in this first-cycle age-31 case is somewhat discretionary rather than strongly guideline-driven.

Provides clear next steps for current transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support adherence, hydrosalpinx evaluation, and uterine reassessment if failure occurs. Useful and practical, though not highly tailored beyond standard IVF management.
